# Didache Chapter 4 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Hierosolymitanus (H), Didache 4 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/DID_004_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 4

**1** Child, keep the memory of your teacher — the one who brings you God's word — before you every day and night. Honor that person as you would honor the Lord himself, because wherever the Lord's authority is spoken, the Lord is there.

**2** Make a point of being with God's people every day. Let their words be a place of rest for you.

**3** Don't cause divisions — be a peacemaker between people who are fighting. When you correct someone, be fair. Don't play favorites.

**4** Don't let doubt paralyze you — don't keep second-guessing whether things will work out.

**5** Don't be the kind of person who's quick to hold out a hand for receiving but slow to open it for giving.

**6** Whatever you earn with your hands — give some of it as an offering for your sins.

**7** Give freely and give gladly. No hesitation, no grumbling. You know who keeps the accounts and pays the reward.

**8** Never turn away someone in need. Share everything you have with your fellow believer — don't treat it as yours alone. After all, if you share eternal life together, how much more should you share earthly goods?

**9** Don't neglect your children. Teach them to fear God from the time they are young.

**10** If you own slaves, don't treat them harshly — they trust in the same God you do. Don't drive them away from God. Remember, he doesn't play favorites when it comes to calling people; he goes to those the Spirit has prepared.

**11** And if you are a slave — serve your master as you would serve God. With humility and respect.

**12** Despise hypocrisy in all its forms. Despise anything that displeases the Lord.

**13** Don't walk away from the Lord's commandments. Guard what you've been entrusted with. Don't add to it. Don't subtract from it.

**14** When the community gathers, confess your sins openly. Don't show up to pray while carrying a guilty conscience. That is the way of life.

---

*PNEUMA note: Chapter 4 is the most socially concrete chapter of the Two Ways section. It addresses money, parenting, slavery, and community discipline. The instructions to both slaveholders (v.10) and enslaved persons (v.11) sit in tension — the Didache doesn't abolish the institution, but it places it under radical theological constraint. The final phrase "This is the way of life" closes the entire Two Ways section (chs. 1–4).*
